newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU delays decision over rice import duties.
newsitem.headline: EU delays decision over rice import duties.

text.p: European Union agricultural experts postponed a vote, possibly until next week, on a new rice import system, EU sources said on Friday.
"A new text was examined but there was nothing very new in it," said one, adding that many member states had objections.
Producer countries -- Italy, Spain, Greece and Portugal -- object in principle to a proposed cumulative recovery system allowing traders to reclaim overpaid duties.
Producer and other EU member states are also unhappy with proposed management and control measures, saying they would not prevent fraud.

Trade sources said that the EU must make a move before the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) meets on March 20 to hear a long-standing U.S. complaint against EU import tariffs for grain, including rice.
The U.S. argues that the tariffs infringe agreements made under the GATT Uruguay Round of world trade talks.
